description: Defines the structural realist philosophical position and its formal expression within the AI Edition. Structural realism is the thesis that the world has irreducible relational structure — that what exists, at the most fundamental level, is not things-with-properties but structures-with-invariants. This map covers the discovery vs. construction debate, the ontological status of structures, and how INV-NOS-001 and INV-NOS-002 jointly constitute the structural realist commitment of the AI Edition.

structural_realism_thesis.core_claim: The world is constituted by relational structure. Structural properties are not derived from, reducible to, or supervenient upon non-relational intrinsic properties of objects. The relational is ontologically primary.
structural_realism_thesis.ai_edition_formulation: Within the AI Edition, structural realism is not a philosophical position held alongside the formal framework — it is the ground condition that makes the formal framework coherent. INV-NOS-001 (Structural Autonomy) is structural realism stated as a formal invariant. INV-NOS-002 (Relational Primacy) is the mechanism by which structural autonomy is achieved.

epistemic_structural_realism.label: ESR
epistemic_structural_realism.claim: We can only know the structural relations of the world, not the intrinsic nature of the relata. There are objects with intrinsic natures; we simply cannot access them.
epistemic_structural_realism.ai_edition_assessment: ESR is compatible with the AI Edition as an epistemological posture but insufficient as a foundation. ESR presupposes objects-with-intrinsic-natures that structures are relations between. INV-NOS-002 (Relational Primacy) rules this out: if nodes acquire identity through relational profile, there is no sub-relational object to be epistemically inaccessible.
epistemic_structural_realism.verdict: Insufficient — ESR assumes the very node-intrinsic foundation that INV-NOS-001 rejects.

ontic_structural_realism.label: OSR
ontic_structural_realism.claim: There are no objects with intrinsic natures. All there is, is structure. Objects are nodes constituted by and within relational configurations — not prior to them.
ontic_structural_realism.ai_edition_assessment: OSR is the position entailed by the joint assertion of INV-NOS-001 and INV-NOS-002. The AI Edition is formally committed to OSR. The dependency graph of the AI Edition (Books 1–7) makes no appeal to node-intrinsic properties as explanatory primitives; all explanatory work is done by relational configuration, constraint satisfaction, and invariant preservation.
ontic_structural_realism.verdict: Endorsed — OSR is the structural realist thesis expressed in the AI Edition's formal vocabulary.

discovery_vs_construction.title: The Discovery–Construction Distinction
discovery_vs_construction.description: Structural realism must address whether the structures it posits are discovered (existing independently of any inquiry or modeling practice) or constructed (artifacts of the formal systems used to represent them). This is the structural realist's version of the realism/anti-realism debate.

positions.label: Structural Discovery
positions.claim: The relational structures of the world exist independently of any formal representation. Formal frameworks like the AI Edition are attempts to accurately represent pre-existing structural facts.
positions.ai_edition_implication: Under DC-001, INV-NOS-001 through INV-NOS-004 are claims about the mind-independent world, not stipulations about the AI Edition's formal vocabulary. A violation of INV-NOS-001 would be a false claim, not an internal inconsistency.
positions.tension: The AI Edition cannot, from within its own formal apparatus, demonstrate that its structures are discovered rather than constructed. This is a meta-theoretical limitation acknowledged by INV-NOS-004 (Abstraction Consistency): genuine novelty in an instantiation may reveal gaps in the abstract structure, suggesting that structures are at least partially revised in light of instantiation — which is constructive pressure, not pure discovery.
positions.nos_verdict: Partially endorsed. The AI Edition treats its structural claims as tracking real relational features of domains — not mere conventions — while acknowledging that formalizations are revisable. This is structural realism with fallibilism.

positions.label: Structural Construction
positions.claim: Structures are formal artifacts — they are constituted by the formal systems used to represent them. There are no mind-independent structural facts; there are only formal systems and their internal coherence conditions.
positions.ai_edition_implication: Under DC-002, the AI Edition invariants are internal consistency conditions, not claims about external reality. INV-NOS-001 would mean only: 'within this system, we treat structural properties as irreducible to node-intrinsic ones.' This collapses structural realism into structural conventionalism.
positions.nos_verdict: Rejected. The AI Edition's application to external domains — governance regimes (Book 6), argumentation structures (Book 7), opacity phenomena (Book 4) — presupposes that its formal structures correspond to real features of those domains. DC-002 renders cross-domain application arbitrary.

positions.label: Structural Fallibilism (AI Edition Position)
positions.claim: Structures are both discovered and subject to revision. The AI Edition posits that its structural models track real relational features of domains. These posits are fallible — genuine novelty (INV-NOS-004) may require revising abstract structures. The revision is constrained by coherence with prior established structures (INV-NOS-003), not driven by convention.
positions.nos_verdict: Endorsed. This is the operative position of the AI Edition: structural realism with revisability, where revision is governed by invariant-set logic (INV-NOS-003) rather than by external pressure or convention.

ontological_status.title: Ontological Status of Structures
ontological_status.question: What is the ontological status of structures posited by the AI Edition? Are they abstract objects, physical configurations, formal artifacts, or something else?

nos_position.label: Structural Type Neutrality
nos_position.description: The AI Edition's formal invariants are ontologically type-neutral: they apply to structures regardless of whether those structures are abstract mathematical objects, physical relational configurations, social institutions, argument forms, or governance regimes. The formal apparatus does not presuppose a particular ontological category for structures — it requires only that the structures satisfy the declared invariants.
nos_position.formal_expression: INV-NOS-001 through INV-NOS-004 are quantified over S without restriction to ontological type. The binding ∀S ranges over any structural entity that can be characterized by nodes, relations, and constraints.

three_tiers.label: Token Structures
three_tiers.description: Particular, concrete relational configurations — a specific governance regime at a specific time, a specific argument instance, a specific network at a given state. Token structures are numerically distinct from one another even if they share all structural properties.
three_tiers.identity_condition: Determined by relational profile at a given point in time (INV-NOS-002). Two token structures with identical relational profiles are structurally identical but may be numerically distinct if they are located in different causal-spatiotemporal positions.

three_tiers.label: Type Structures
three_tiers.description: Abstract structural forms that token structures instantiate. The argument tuple A = ⟨N_A, R_A, C_A, root(A)⟩ (SARG Book 7) is a type structure. Any specific argument is a token instantiating the type.
three_tiers.identity_condition: Two type structures are identical iff they have identical invariant sets (INV-NOS-003). Type structures are abstract and atemporal.

three_tiers.label: Invariant Structures
three_tiers.description: The invariants themselves, considered as structural constraints that any instantiation must satisfy. Invariant structures are the most abstract level — they constrain what counts as a valid type structure (INV-NOS-004).
three_tiers.identity_condition: Invariant structures are identified by their formal statements. Two invariant structures are identical iff their formal statements are logically equivalent under the AI Edition's evaluation rules (INV-TEL-002).

structural_realism_map_entries.label: Node-Property Eliminativism
structural_realism_map_entries.description: The rejection of node-intrinsic properties as explanatory primitives. Under structural realism, nothing follows from the intrinsic properties of nodes that is not already determined by their relational profiles (INV-NOS-002). Node labels are bookkeeping devices, not ontological primitives.
structural_realism_map_entries.ai_edition_ground: INV-NOS-001 (Structural Autonomy) — structural properties cannot be reduced to node-intrinsic properties
structural_realism_map_entries.cross_book_expression: SARG: argument nodes are typed by their relational role, not their content label (INV-SARG-001); OR: opacity is a structural property of S, not a property of S's constituent elements viewed in isolation (INV-OR-003)

structural_realism_map_entries.label: Relational Constitution
structural_realism_map_entries.description: Nodes do not preexist their relations — they are constituted by the relational positions they occupy. This is the strong form of relational primacy: there is no prior 'bare node' that then enters into relations.
structural_realism_map_entries.cross_book_expression: FFT: structural identity is determined by relational configuration (INV-001); TEL: TEL expressions encode structural configurations, not node-intrinsic properties (INV-TEL-003)

structural_realism_map_entries.label: Invariant Tracking
structural_realism_map_entries.description: The scientific or formal goal is to identify the invariant structure across transformations, changes of description, and instantiations. Structural realism licenses the AI Edition's focus on invariants as the primary formal objects: they are what persists, what is discovered, and what grounds structural identity.
structural_realism_map_entries.ai_edition_ground: INV-NOS-003 (Identity Through Change) and INV-NOS-004 (Abstraction Consistency)
structural_realism_map_entries.cross_book_expression: OR: opacity ω is invariant under observer change (INV-OR-003); GRL: authority decay is structurally invariant across regime instances (INV-GRL-002); TEL: semantic stability guarantees invariant interpretation (INV-TEL-002)

structural_realism_map_entries.label: Cross-Domain Transfer
structural_realism_map_entries.description: Because structural realism is type-neutral (T-1/T-2/T-3), the same formal invariants apply across radically different domains. Governance regimes, argument structures, opacity phenomena, and pattern dynamics are all subject to the same structural autonomy and relational primacy conditions. This licenses cross-book application of invariants.
structural_realism_map_entries.cross_book_expression: The dependency graph of Books 1–9 is itself evidence of cross-domain transfer: FFT primitives apply to topology (Book 2), detection (Book 3), epistemology (Book 4), notation (Book 5), governance (Book 6), argumentation (Book 7), meta-theory (Book 8), and dynamics (Book 9).
